subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

spec.name: Lionheart Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style gunblade in the manner of Squall's Revolver: a broad single-edged blade whose spine is a gun barrel, a revolver cylinder and hammer at the base, a trigger grip, and a silver lion pendant on a chain, standing pommel-down on the floor.
spec.layout: One static weapon, blade up, pommel resting on y=0, centred on x=0 and standing in the x–y plane. The broad flat faces of the blade point to ±Z and the viewer at +Z sees the full blade side. The cutting edge is on +X (the model's left). The spine and barrel are on -X. The trigger guard loop and the pendant are also on +X. Reading bottom to top: a round pommel cap (y 0–0.07), a leather-wrapped grip (y 0.07–0.34) with a steel collar and trigger loop (y 0.22–0.40), a gold crossguard (y 0.40–0.46), the gunmetal receiver with the revolver cylinder, hammer and a glowing blue core (y 0.46–0.74), then the blade (y 0.72–1.45). The blade has a thick spine housing the barrel on -X, a central fuller groove, bright bevelled edge strips, an engraved gold inlay line, a small run of glowing cyan runes and a clipped angled tip with a swept notch near the top. The lion head medallion hangs on a chain from the guard's +X wing and stays beside the trigger loop at about y 0.17. Style: Final Fantasy. The shapes are bold and ornate, with an elegant tall silhouette. Polished steel in two or three tones (light top bevels, darker fuller and underside), gold filigree trim, dark gunmetal mechanics, small crimson and cyan accents, and glow on the core, the chamber rim and the runes. Every detail is a small part in its own colour sitting on the surface: rivets, bolts, engraving lines, chamber holes and bevel strips. All parts are blocky and faceted, with 6–10 sided cylinders.

parts.builds: The handle, centred on x=0, z=0, with its axis along Y. A round pommel cap (gold, dark gold ring below it, 8-sided, radius about 0.04) and a short tapered pommel spike or ring plate. Grip y 0.07–0.34: a leather-brown core (leather, radius about 0.03) with diagonal leatherWrap strips wound round it (small angled boxes or a stack of thin rings), plus two gold ferrules. A steel collar at y 0.34–0.40 with a gold band. A trigger guard: a thin loop in the XY plane (swept rod, steel, radius 0.006) from the collar at about y 0.40, out to x 0.11 and back to the grip at y 0.22. Inside it hangs a small crescent trigger in gunmetal. Tiny gold rivets on the collar and a small crimson gem on the pommel front (+Z).
parts.attaches: Its top ends at the gripTop mount (y 0.40) under the crossguard of the receiver part. The trigger loop meets the grip at triggerLoop. Its lowest point, the pommelBase, rests on y=0.

parts.builds: The crossguard and the gun mechanism, y 0.40–0.74. The gold crossguard is a wide flat bar at y 0.40–0.46, from x -0.12 to 0.13 and z ±0.045. Its +X wing sweeps up and out into a feathered gold wing shape with a hole or hook at chainAttach, and its -X end is a smaller upturned wing. It has goldDark trim lines and goldLight tips. The receiver above is a gunmetal block (x -0.10..0.06, z ±0.06, y 0.46..0.72) with chamfered plates in gunmetalLight, ink panel seams and bolts. The revolver cylinder sits on the spine side at cylinderCenter (-0.05, 0.60, 0): an upright 8-sided drum with radius 0.05 and height 0.13, steel with six dark ink chamber holes on its +Z face, gold top and bottom rims, and tiny glowCyan chamber rim dots. Behind it a hammer: a gunmetal angled block with a gold tip pivoting at hammerPivot (-0.1, 0.70, 0) on the -X side. A glowing royalBlue/glowCyan core gem on the +Z receiver face at about (0.0, 0.56, 0.062), set in a gold bezel. The barrel root is a gunmetal tube housing at x -0.095..-0.05 which rises into the blade's spine at the top (y 0.74). Also a small ejector rod on the cylinder side and screw heads.
parts.attaches: Sits on gripTop (y 0.40). The blade's ricasso and spine enter its top at bladeBase (y 0.72). Its +X wing holds chainAttach for the ornaments part.

parts.builds: The blade from y 0.72 to tip y 1.45, centred on x≈0. It has flat faces toward ±Z and is about 0.035 thick in z in the middle. Width runs from the spine at x -0.07 to the cutting edge at x +0.075. It is built as a stack or extrude of a single-edged outline: a straight spine, a slight belly on the edge, a clipped angled point (the tip swept up toward -X) and a small notch step near y 1.30 on the edge side. The steel body is in steel with a darker steelDark fuller groove (a long inset strip, x -0.02..0.02, z faces) from y 0.8 to 1.3, inside which a thin goldLight inlay line and a few glowCyan rune ticks (3–5 small glyph parts) are seated. Edge bevel strips in steelLight and edgeWhite run the full length on +X on both faces. A thick spine on -X is a gunmetal barrel-housing bar (x -0.095..-0.05, z ±0.025) from the receiver up to y 1.2, with a muzzle block and gold muzzle ring near its end at y 1.2–1.25, and small gunmetalLight sight nubs. Gold ricasso bands and tiny rivets near the base (y 0.72–0.80). A short dark ink notch line below the tip and some slim steelDark scratch accents.
parts.attaches: Its base enters the receiver at bladeBase (y 0.72, centred x 0). The spine housing continues the receiver's barrel at spineLine. The tip is at bladeTip, the highest point of the model (y 1.45).

parts.builds: The ornament on the +X side. It hangs from the chainAttach mount (0.12, 0.44, 0): a small gold ring, then a chain of about 8–10 tiny linked beads or boxes in chainGrey, alternating orientation, drooping with a slight curve outward to x 0.15 at y 0.24. At pendantCenter (0.15, 0.17, 0) hangs the lion head medallion, facing +Z, about 0.065 tall. A round silver disc (lionSilver, radius 0.032, 10 sides) with a gold rim and a raised lion face made of small parts: a mane of 8–10 spiky silver/steelDark triangular blades radiating round it, a muzzle block, two ink eyes with tiny gold highlights, a small ink nose and a goldDark brow. Below it hang two short crimson ribbon tails (flat thin boxes, one with a swallow-tail end) and a tiny gold bead. Next to the chain, tied round the +X crossguard wing, is a short crimson ribbon knot. Keep every piece clear of the trigger loop (which reaches x 0.115) and above y 0.05 so it clears the floor.
parts.attaches: Attached to the receiver's +X guard wing at chainAttach. The pendant medallion center is the pendantCenter mount.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a Final Fantasy-style gunblade, Squall's Revolver-like, as a static model with no joints, planted point-down so its tip touches the floor at y=0.

Actually I think the pommel-down orientation reads more iconic, with the blade pointing up and the grip resting on the floor at a total length of about 1.4m — cutting edge on +X, spine on -X, with the revolver cylinder and barrel mounted along the spine near the base of the blade and the trigger guard positioned below at the grip.

Now I'm laying out the full dimensions: grip, pommel, and trigger assembly spanning roughly y 0 to 0.42, with the trigger guard extending toward the edge side (+X) since the blade's flat face points toward the viewer (+Z) and the edge faces left.

Continuing upward, the receiver/gun mechanism housing sits around y 0.40-0.75, then the blade runs y 0.62-1.45, tapering from a wider base to a swept clipped point at the tip, with a spine rim, fuller groove, and light edge bevel. For ornamentation I'm planning a "Crest & Trim" piece: a lion-head pendant with chain, engraved runes, and emblems to echo the Revolver's iconic lion motif on the guard.

I'm working out a draping chain from the guard's side loop down to a lion-head medallion pendant, plus glowing blue magic gems embedded in the receiver and cylinder. I'm settling on four parts -- grip, mechanism, blade, and ornaments -- with a budget split of 150/200/250/150 for 750 total, and picking out a steel, gunmetal, gold, and leather color palette.

Now I'm placing mount points: grip-to-receiver junction, receiver center, blade base, guard center, and the revolver cylinder, reasoning through how the cylinder's axis should run parallel to the blade like a real gunblade design.

I'm recentering the blade geometry so the centerline sits near x=0, adjusting the pendant and spine offsets so the overall bounding box spans roughly -0.15 to 0.17 in width.

Now I'm defining the orientation convention: blade flats facing ±Z, edge at +X, spine at -X, lion pendant facing +Z, with the trigger guard loop lying flat in the XY plane and extending outward toward +X before curving back down to the grip, and the pendant chain attaching near the guard's outer edge.

I'm laying out the pommel, grip, trigger loop, and collar segments, then stacking the crossguard, receiver body with its hammer, and the blade ricasso up through the tip, defining the floor and spatial bounds for each part as I go.

Grouping ornaments next: a lion medallion, chain, and a feather or ribbon tassel tied near the pommel's lanyard ring, making sure the tassel stays above the floor line rather than hanging below zero.
